tagline: every host, labelled and kept on purpose
subtitle: How a host enters the catalog, how its category is decided, how the shipped file is built from the seeds, and how a release is verified. Every node below is a real script or file in the repository.
audience: Engineers onboarding onto the catalog build and release path

flows.name: Ingest — how a host gets a label
flows.note: A source carries names, never categories; a rule or a person decides the label.

steps.title: Pull a trusted list
steps.desc: The harvester fetches a list already cleared in the registry. It sends no key, no cookie and no account — the publisher cannot tell who asked.
steps.payload:
GET https://…/hosts
If-None-Match: "<etag>"

# no Authorization, no cookie, no query string

steps.title: The licence gate
steps.desc: sources.py refuses a non-commercial or blocked licence before a single name is stored. The refusal is keyed on the licence, not on a list of names, so the next NC source is refused without anyone adding it.
steps.payload:
sources.py: licence == MIT   → allow
             licence == NC    → refuse

# the gate is a table, not a changelog

steps.title: A person labels it
steps.desc: A category is a decision, never a guess. It is either a rule in rules.json or a person who wrote down a reason. The host's page is never asked to invent one.
steps.payload:
rules.json:
  drop.hosts["banco.com"] = "closed"

# or a hand-added line with by / at / reason

steps.title: The seeds are the source of truth
steps.desc: catalog.json is a build output. Every change lands in seeds/ first, and the shipped file is rebuilt from it — so a reviewer reads a seed diff, not a data diff.

flows.name: Verify — is the host still real?
flows.note: Three independent checks, two rounds, and an intersection — one signal never removes a host.

steps.title: Three independent checks
steps.desc: DNS asks nine questions; the live sweep reads the page; the registration sweep asks a registrar. They are independent on purpose, so no single failure can remove a good host.
steps.payload:
probe-dead.py          # nine DNS questions
sweep-live.py          # parked / empty / real
verify-registrations.py # who owns it now

steps.title: Agreement, not a single signal
steps.desc: Two rounds must agree before anything is proposed. Unsure keeps the host — an empty 200 or a flaky TCP failure is common on live infrastructure.
steps.payload:
round 1 == round 2  → propose removal
round 1 != round 2  → keep (unsure)

# a single signal never removes

steps.title: A removal is written down
steps.desc: Nothing leaves because a sweep said so. The removal becomes an entry in rules.json → drop.hosts with a reason and a date — a decision a person can audit.
steps.payload:
rules.json → drop.hosts
  host:   "old-bank.com.tr"
  reason: "gone, two rounds agree"
  date:   "2026-10-15"

steps.title: Nothing returns quietly
steps.desc: The dropped host is absent from the seeds, and a check proves it — so a later harvest that lists it again cannot silently restore it.
steps.payload:
# test/test.sh
checked N dropped host(s)
  are absent from the seeds

steps.title: Unlabelled stays unlabelled
steps.desc: A host a source listed that no rule matches is an open question, not a row. Writing it as other would turn the question into a claim, and on screen other looks like an answer.
steps.payload:
# guides/NEEDS-REVIEW.md
host, what was tried, what happened

# in neither seeds nor catalog.json

flows.name: Build — from seeds to shipped file
flows.note: catalog.json is a pure function of the seeds: regenerate, and the diff is empty unless something really changed.

steps.title: Rebuild from the seeds
steps.desc: The generator reads the seeds and the rules and writes catalog.json. It validates before it writes, so a bad seed writes nothing — there is never a half-written catalog.

steps.title: Deterministic by construction
steps.desc: Hosts are sorted, services are sorted by key and the indent is fixed, so the same seeds build the same bytes. A rebuild diff is a real change, never a reshuffle.
steps.payload:
normalize(doc)
  categories: {host: category}  # sorted
  services:   sorted by key
  indent:     2

steps.title: catalog.json
steps.desc: One JSON file, about 232 KB, carrying the category of every kept host and the service table. This is the artifact a consumer reads.
steps.payload:
catalog.json
  version:    1
  generated:  date
  categories: 6731
  services:   22

steps.title: Measure the labels
steps.desc: The reliability audit reads each host's own page and recovers the label with a text model. It measures the labels; it never writes them. A low score is a label worth a look, not a wrong one.

steps.title: A checksum travels with it
steps.desc: manifest.json records the SHA-256 and size of the exact bytes shipped. A consumer pulls the kilobyte manifest first, and only fetches the catalog when it changed — then verifies the hash.
steps.payload:
scripts/release/build-manifest.py
  sha256(catalog.json)
  bytes, size
→ manifest.json  (~232 B)

flows.name: Verify & ship — nothing leaves red
flows.note: A release pins a tag by hand, and every gate has already passed on the same bytes.

steps.title: Every gate runs
steps.desc: One command runs the whole suite: the registry, the seeds, the hand-edit traps, the build, the validation and the documentation freshness. It is the single definition of "green".
steps.payload:
./test/test.sh
  registry → seeds → build
  → validate → docs → release

steps.title: Docs cannot drift
steps.desc: The generated documents are rebuilt and compared byte for byte. If a regenerate moves anything, the run fails — a hand edit is caught rather than tolerated.
steps.payload:
build-catalog-docs.py --check
build-coverage.py     --check
→ stale docs fail the run

steps.title: The file validates
steps.desc: The built catalog is checked against its own schema: the version, the services and every host. A document that does not validate never reaches a release.

steps.title: A manual run publishes the bytes
steps.desc: A maintainer starts the release workflow from the Actions tab; it creates the tag and attaches the catalog and its manifest. The moving main always points at the current file; a tag never moves.
steps.payload:
.github/workflows/release.yml
workflow_dispatch vX.Y.Z
→ GitHub Release
   catalog.json
   manifest.json

steps.title: Consumers verify before they pull
steps.desc: Another application reads the manifest, compares the hash, and pulls the catalog only when it actually changed. The contract for that is in the reference docs.
steps.payload:
GET …/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/
  manifest.json   (~232 B)
  catalog.json    (~232 KB)

verify sha256, then read
